workspace.description: Optional language settings for a workspace without a registry: report_language is the language of the report to the owner (absent means the user's own language; everything else written is English); language_allow lists path globs for localisation data that the english-only advisories skip.

pipeline.description: Delivery pipeline (scripts/factory-pipeline.py, policy skills/delivery/references/delivery.md, RPG specifics in skills/factory-core/references/parallel-work.md): task tiers, the agents that implement and review, cross-model review pairing and shared exclusive resources.

XS.flow: run lead writes a one-task plan with tier XS; every owned path is prose; the run lead edits the files itself on the plan topic branch and commits with explicit paths; dispatch --phase review --sha <sha> runs one cross-model review (implementer recorded as the run lead's model); the run lead runs the task tier command and records verdict --phase qa --by <lead model> --note "tier XS: lead ran task suites"; gate; PR; no task lead, task worktree or implement session

S.flow: run lead writes a one-task plan.json; validate; dispatch --phase lead starts the task lead (task worktree; no-worktree repo: main checkout); task lead runs sub-sessions, cross-model review and QA; run lead integrates (never implements); gate; PR

M.flow: run lead writes plan.json; validate; dispatch --phase lead per task (one task lead each; no-worktree repo: main checkout, in sequence); task leads run sub-sessions, cross-model review and QA; run lead integrates; integration QA; gate; PR

L.flow: planner worker writes plan.json; validate; dispatch --phase lead per task in waves (one task lead each; no-worktree repo: main checkout, in sequence); task leads run sub-sessions, cross-model review and QA; run lead integrates; integration QA per repo; gate; one PR per repo

qa_tiers.description: Task QA runs affected and explicit check suites once; integration runs tests/run-all.sh --workspace-only locally; CI runs the affected suites per change and ci-ok must be green before merging (every suite through workflow_dispatch with full=true).

models.description: Model policy: scope = what may run at all (agent -> model -> allowed efforts); profiles = the model and effort of each role and grade; every profile is inside scope. A personal override file may narrow scope and replace profiles (scripts/lib/model_policy.py; policy: skills/delivery/references/delivery.md section 10 'Model choice').

rubric.light: Mechanical or well-bounded change: rename, typo, doc or text edit, config value, one small function, a test that copies an existing pattern; the answer is obvious from the surrounding code.
rubric.standard: Ordinary feature or fix inside one module that follows existing patterns and needs some design, new tests and a few connected files.
rubric.heavy: Hard or risky change: contract, wire or generated paths, concurrency, ECS or tick-loop internals, security or data migration, cross-module refactor, or anything where a wrong guess is costly to find.

subagents.description: In-session subagents are read-only scouts; per role: access, max parallel and when to use one (policy: skills/delivery/references/delivery.md section 8 'In-session subagents'; rule text: scripts/lib/subagent_policy.py).

run_lead.when: the answer needs many files or an open search and only the conclusion matters

planner.when: the plan needs facts from many files or repos and only the conclusion matters

lead.when: the task needs a broad search across the worktree and only the conclusion matters

implement.when: the change needs a search across many files that would crowd the context and only the conclusion matters

review.when: a claim in the diff needs a check across many files and only the finding matters

qa.when: never: QA runs the checks itself and grades the evidence
